rule: Show live, blocked, and next before any workflow opens.
purpose: Keep Heavyster calm as the product grows by showing one role-aware launch pulse before deeper workflows.
phase_one_guardrail: No rental payment collection, escrow, payout, deposit, or commission workflow in phase one. Heavyster earns listing SaaS while the buyer pays the supplier directly.

role_pulses.live: Marketplace search, proof card, route clarity, and direct enquiry are usable now.
role_pulses.blocked: Saved buyer account, RFQ history, quote history, and booking audit trail need backend records.
role_pulses.money: 0% rental take. The buyer pays the rental company directly.
role_pulses.next: Use the cleanest visible machine path and copy one enquiry.

role_pulses.live: Listing workspace, proof checklist, revenue preview, and direct lead path are visible now.
role_pulses.blocked: Supplier login, uploads, billing checkout, real listing CRUD, and permissions need backend records.
role_pulses.money: USD 9 monthly or USD 99 yearly per active listing. Rental payment remains direct.
role_pulses.next: Confirm availability and publish one paid-ready listing.

role_pulses.live: Market command shows demand, supply, proof, direct enquiry, and listing ARR signals.
role_pulses.blocked: Auth, database, storage, billing, admin review, and lead history are production gates.
role_pulses.money: Listing ARR first. Success fees wait until Heavyster proves the booking workflow.
role_pulses.next: Fill the highest-priority supply gap before pushing traffic.

acceptance: Header and Build Phase both show v149.
Marketplace, Supplier Studio, Pricing, Build Phase, and Roadmap can show a role-aware launch pulse.
Pulse always includes Live, Blocked, Money, and Next states.
Primary action opens one safe next screen for the active role.
Copy action creates a plain text operating pulse for buyer, supplier, or founder.
No pulse action introduces rental checkout, escrow, payout, deposit, or commission handling.
Build Phase includes a v149 Calm Launch Pulse contract.
Static check verifies the JSON contract, public UI hooks, app renderer, and CSS hooks.
